answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions behind a bonded reputation: each identity locks scarce tokens, then earns a higher limit only after completing jobs whose outcomes are checked by counterparties and recorded on-chain. A long horizon makes the bond and accumulated history an anchor, while splitting into fresh identities resets that history. The timber is the capital tied up in every identity; if fraud is detected, slashing destroys the bond, so a Sybil attacker must fund many accounts and risk losing each stake.
